title: Day 79: ACLED Report — CJNG Maintains Military Power & Criminal Revenues Post-Mencho; El Sapo Hunt Continues; 30 Days to FIFA World Cup
detail: Day 79 since El Mencho's killing at Tapalpa, Jalisco (February 22, 2026). ACLED ASSESSMENT (May 12, 2026): The Armed Conflict Location & Event Data project (ACLED) published a major analysis today in Proceso concluding that 79 days after El Mencho's death, there is zero evidence the CJNG has fractured or that rival cartels — including the Sinaloa Cartel — have capitalized on the leadership vacuum. ACLED Latin America chief analyst Sandra Pellegrini describes the organization as showing 'tactical containment' and organizational adaptation, with no verifiable successor publicly established. Notably, ACLED found that CJNG has reinforced alliances in Michoacán with Los Viagras — a historically adversarial relationship — suggesting the O3-led administration is managing territorial exposure by co-opting former rivals rather than fighting on all fronts simultaneously. A companion El Imparcial analysis published the same day asks why the CJNG empire has not collapsed despite 79 consecutive days of decapitation campaign pressure, noting the cartel's franchise model enables autonomous cell operation regardless of central leadership disruption. EL SAPO HUNT — DAY 79: Hugo Gonzalo Mendoza Gaytán 'El Sapo' ('El 090') remains Mexico's Federal Security Cabinet top-priority CJNG enforcement target (named May 3). An FGR protected witness — a former FARC Front 30 member who served as El Sapo's escort — testified (file FED/FEMDO/FEITATAJAL/0001023/2024) that 'when El Mencho is gone, El 090 will take it all.' His personal security detail includes former Mexican Army, Marines, and Colombian and Guatemalan former combatants — making capture operations high-risk. As CJNG's military chief, El Sapo retains active control of sicario recruitment networks in Jalisco, Michoacán, and Puebla, and manages the Puerto Vallarta-Manzanillo fentanyl precursor corridor logistics despite the May 9 El Chucky arrest. POST-EL CHUCKY MANZANILLO VOID (Day 3): Three days after Lorenzo Sánchez 'El Chucky' was arrested May 9, the Port of Manzanillo's CJNG plaza command structure remains in transition. No successor plaza boss has been publicly identified. CJNG's embedded port relationships (corrupted customs officials, dock workers, shipping intermediaries) remain structurally intact. Analysts assess El 03's Grupo Élite will designate a replacement within 1–2 weeks. The ACLED report's finding of continued CJNG organizational integrity is consistent with this transition assessment. DECAPITATION LEDGER — DAY 79: El Mencho (killed Feb 22), El Tuli (killed Feb 22), El Doble R (arrested March 11), El Jardinero (arrested April 27, vinculado a proceso at Altiplano May 4), El Güero Conta (arrested April 27), El Cabo (arrested May 7), El Chucky/Manzanillo plaza boss (arrested May 9). Operativo Enjambre: 80+ officials detained. PLAN KUKULKAN — 30 DAYS: Mexico's FIFA World Cup 2026 security strategy enters the 30-day threshold. Guadalajara (Akron Stadium) hosts 4 group-stage matches. Mexico's 130,000-person nationwide security deployment continues. QUINTUPLE BILATERAL PRESSURE — DAY 79: (1) CIA-Chihuahua sovereignty deadlock; (2) DOJ SDNY indictment of Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya + 9 officials ('temporary leave' since May 2); (3) Sheinbaum's 'irrefutable proof' extradition standard (May 6); (4) U.S. State Dept review of 53 Mexican consulates; (5) ongoing CJNG interdiction. Trump's May 7 warning ('if they're not gonna do the job, we will') remains the maximum rhetorical escalation point. SUCCESSION BINARY: El 03 (financial wing, confirmed leader) vs. El Sapo (military wing, at large) — ACLED assessment that CJNG has not fractured validates the O3 consolidation narrative, even as El Sapo's continued freedom sustains the internal military-wing succession tension.
